- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model frequently underestimates continuation; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for momentum bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; apply +1–2% bias to forecast if sentiment < -0.20.
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive (e.g., from -0.50 to -0.10), model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% in first 2–3 days of sentiment shift.
- Avoid over-relying on recent 30-day trend; if sentiment is volatile or mixed, use 18-day history as anchor and adjust forecast ±0.5–1.0% based on sentiment direction.
